chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ziyad ibn Marwan, who said:
I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about completing the prayer in the two Holy Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), so he said: 'I like for you what I like for myself: complete the prayer.'

key_terms.أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِتْمَامِ الصَّلَاةِ: Completing the prayer (praying four rak'ahs instead of two)
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Holy Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for completing or shortening prayer in Mecca and Medina according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Ziyad ibn Marwan seeks the ruling of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding whether to shorten (*qasr*) or complete (*tamm*) the four-rak'ah prayer while in the Holy Sanctuaries of Mecca and Medina. The Imam’s response, 'I love for you what I love for myself,' is interpreted by Shia jurists as a strong recommendation (*istihbab*) to perform the full four-rak'ah prayer, distinguishing the sanctity of these locations from the general rule of shortening prayers during travel.
